clue.text: Chinese leader was ecstatic -he had a yen

indicators.note: the first letter of the word it picks from

parts.note: the leading letter of the word Chinese is C
to rave is to enthuse wildly, so was ecstatic gives raved

explanation.surface: A Chinese leader was overjoyed because he was holding some Japanese currency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yen' looks like the Japanese money beside 'Chinese'; here it is a longing. 'he' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a yen is to long or hanker for something, the past tense matching.

clue.text: Record extra rescheduling of debt

parts.note: a roll is a record or register, as in a roll call
over means extra or surplus, as in left over

explanation.surface: A notable additional rearrangement of what is owed.
explanation.definitionFit: A rollover extends a loan by refinancing it for a further term.

clue.text: Serviceman on time at his home

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: a vicar is a man who conducts church services
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A soldier at home on time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Serviceman' looks like a soldier; it is a clergyman who takes services. 'at' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A vicarage is the house provided for the parish priest.

clue.text: Vandal does conceal his booty

indicators.note: the deer hide the booty within them

parts.note: does are female deer, and deer is also plural
spoil is plunder or booty

explanation.surface: A vandal does hide his loot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'does' looks like a verb; it is the plural of doe, giving DEER. 'his' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A despoiler plunders or ruins things, much as a vandal wrecks property.

clue.text: Money recovered is returned on the nail

indicators.note: in a down-style placement one piece sits on the next; here it simply puts one word before the other

parts.note: a claw is an animal's nail
something returned is back

explanation.surface: Cash reclaimed is paid back on the nail, that is, promptly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the nail' looks like the idiom for paying at once; here the nail is an animal's, and 'on' just sets one word before the other. 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A clawback is a sum an authority takes back, such as a recouped tax allowance.

clue.text: Eph. 1:10 can provide the exact 'reference

parts.note: a Bible citation such as Ephesians 1:10 names a book, then two numbers locating the passage precisely

explanation.surface: A Bible citation offering a precise source.
explanation.walkthrough: In Eph. 1:10 the 1 is the chapter and the 10 the verse; the phrase also means a precise source in general.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means full, precise detail of a source, from biblical citation by numbered sections.

clue.text: Want to incarcerate poisoner of uncertain temper

indicators.note: the word for want imprisons the snake inside it

parts.note: to wish is to want
an asp is a venomous snake

explanation.surface: A wish to jail a moody poisoner.
explanation.definitionFit: Waspish means irritable or prickly, quick to take offence.

clue.text: Opening a package of purer tea

indicators.note: packaging rearranges the contents, so the letters of purer tea are shuffled

explanation.surface: Tearing open a packet of high-grade tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'package of' signals rearranging PURER TEA. 'a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperture is a gap or hole, such as a camera's lens opening.

clue.text: One of two books with joint authority

parts.note: the Old Testament has two books of Kings, First and Second
the hip is a joint

explanation.surface: Two books with shared authorship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint' looks like shared; it is the body part. 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Kingship is royal rule, the power and authority of a monarch.

clue.text: Woman is without inside water

indicators.note: signals that the phrase for 'is without' goes within the woman's name

parts.note: Bea is a woman's name
one who is without something lacks it

explanation.surface: A woman is outdoors while the water is inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'outside', a container signal, but it means 'lacking'; the container signal is 'inside'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a named sea between Europe and Asia, a body of water.

clue.text: Like a bird's behind

parts.note: as means like, in a comparison
a tern is a seabird; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: A remark about the tail feathers of some bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind' looks like a noun, a bird's rear; it is the adverb meaning at the back of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Astern is the nautical word for behind or towards the rear of a vessel.

clue.text: Work or job — it's a support, for openers

parts.note: to do is to work
taken as written
a post is a job

explanation.surface: Whether work or a job, it gives support to those starting out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'openers' looks like beginners; it means doors, and the post supports them.
explanation.definitionFit: A doorpost is an upright of the frame on which a door hangs.

clue.text: It's right to stroke gaping beak

parts.note: an ictus is a stroke, a beat or stress in verse or medicine

explanation.surface: It's fine to stroke a bird's open beak.
explanation.walkthrough: ICTUS is an uncommon word for a stroke or beat. 'It's' and 'to' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A rictus is the gape of a bird's mouth, the opening of the bill.

clue.text: Ancient river in flood once drove men west

indicators.note: puts the old river within the word for flood

parts.note: a gush is a sudden flood of liquid
old means ancient
R is the abbreviation for river on maps

explanation.surface: An old river in spate once carried men westward.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition refers to the 1849 California rush that sent prospectors west across America.
explanation.definitionFit: The California gold rush of 1849 lured thousands of prospectors westward in search of fortune.

clue.text: Art is not dead yet

parts.note: still means yet, as in 'still here'
being not dead is to have life

explanation.surface: Art is still alive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link; the phrase reads as a claim that art lives on.
explanation.definitionFit: A still life is a painting of inanimate objects such as fruit or flowers, a genre of art.

clue.text: Indian to make silent progress, almost

indicators.note: the word for silent movement is left short of its final letter

parts.note: to creep is to move silently and slowly

explanation.surface: An Indian moving stealthily, nearly there.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cree are a Native American people of Canada, once called Indians.

clue.text: Stayed unnaturally thin-looking?

parts.note: 'stays' are the boned panels of a tight undergarment, so 'stayed' means laced into one to look slim

explanation.surface: Someone stayed somewhere and oddly looked thin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stayed' seems to mean remained; it means fitted with stays, the whalebone strips of a waist-cinching garment.
explanation.definitionFit: Laced into a stiff bodice to pinch the waist, giving an artificially slim figure.

clue.text: He has no real way out of his difficulties

definitions.text: He has no real way out of his difficulties

parts.words: He has no real way out of his difficulties
parts.note: this person flees problems only through fantasy, an imaginary rather than real exit

explanation.surface: A man trapped in his troubles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'way out' reads as a solution; it is a flight into daydream.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who retreats into fantasy to avoid unpleasant reality.

clue.text: One in permanent employment? Yes and no

definitions.text: One in permanent employment? Yes and no

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the phrase permanent employment, across its two words

explanation.surface: A riddle about someone both in permanent work and not.
explanation.walkthrough: Yes: the word sits inside 'permanent employment'. No: such a worker's job is not permanent.
explanation.definitionFit: A temporary worker is employed but never permanently, hence both yes and no.

clue.text: Harsh arrangement — boy is about to be beaten

indicators.note: the boy's name goes around the rearranged letters

parts.note: Ted is a boy's name

indicators.note: an arrangement reorders the letters of harsh

explanation.surface: A severe set-up: a boy is going to get a beating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement' shuffles the first word, and 'is about' wraps the boy's name around the result. 'to be' is a link; the surface's beaten boy is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrashed means beaten soundly, whether flogged or defeated.

clue.text: Changed head of transport union?

indicators.note: the leading letter of the transport word is swapped for another

parts.note: a carriage is a horse-drawn vehicle, a means of transport

explanation.surface: A new leader for a transport workers' union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transport union' looks like a trade union; the union is wedlock. The new head letter is not clued, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Wedlock is the union of two people.

clue.text: Advertise healthy food?

explanation.surface: A question about promoting wholesome eating.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word into a bran dish, bran being a fibre-rich health food.
explanation.definitionFit: To brandish is to flourish or show off, while a bran dish is wholesome fare.

clue.text: Tame sort of crime

explanation.surface: A mild kind of offence.
explanation.definitionFit: To break in a horse is to tame it, and burglary by forcing entry is a break-in.

clue.text: Got up like an armadillo

explanation.surface: An armadillo-like creature climbing.
explanation.definitionFit: Climbed a wall is scaled, and an armadillo's body is covered in bony plates.

clue.text: Enlightened writer, the creator of Zaire

explanation.surface: An Enlightenment author who appears to have founded an African state.
explanation.walkthrough: Zaïre is a 1732 tragedy by this French writer, not the African country later named Zaire.
explanation.definitionFit: The French author was a leading thinker of the Age of Reason and wrote the play Zaïre.

clue.text: Many card games are so difficult

explanation.surface: Lots of card games are hard to play.
explanation.walkthrough: Many card games, like whist and bridge, are played in tricks.
explanation.definitionFit: Trick-taking games are built around tricks, and the word also means awkward or hard.

clue.text: It's the end of the line for chief, after abuse

definitions.text: It's the end of the line

indicators.note: the word for chief comes after the word for abuse

parts.note: to rail at someone is to abuse them verbally
a head is a chief

explanation.surface: A boss's career ends after a scandal of mistreatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A railhead is the terminus of a railway, the furthest point the track reaches.

clue.text: Set off for appointment — broken by college

indicators.note: the appointment word is split open with the college placed in it

parts.note: a date is an appointment
Eton is the famous English public school, Eton College

explanation.surface: Someone leaves for a meeting that a college interrupts.
explanation.walkthrough: ETON is Eton College, an English boarding school near Windsor. 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To detonate a bomb is to set it off.

clue.text: Supplies charges after men beheaded

indicators.note: the charges come after what remains of men
the word men loses its first letter

parts.note: taken as written before losing its head
dues are fees or charges

explanation.surface: Provisions pay for fees after men are executed.
explanation.definitionFit: To endue is to endow or provide someone with a quality.
